findings.title: New TotalDocs log races with index cache writes
findings.body: The newly added log calls s.search.TotalDocs() after the watch goroutine at lines 207-213 has already been started. bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu, while handleEvent -> getOrCreateIndex -> BuildIndex can write b.cache under cacheMu. This is a data race and can panic at startup with 'concurrent map iteration and map write'. Either make TotalDocs lock cacheMu or evaluate total docs before starting the watcher.

findings.title: Shared err and counter are mutated by concurrent init goroutines
findings.body: Inside searchSupport.init, every errgroup goroutine assigns to the captured outer err variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and returns that same variable, and they also increment totalBatchesIndexed concurrently. These are data races. In particular, another goroutine can overwrite err with nil just before a failing goroutine returns it, so group.Wait can miss a build failure and startup proceeds with a partially built index. Use per-goroutine local errors (or return s.build(...) directly) and an atomic/collected counter.

findings.title: Removing the build lock allows concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu for the duration of the build. getOrCreateIndex performs an unlocked check-then-build, so two callers can both see no index for the same NamespacedResource and enter BuildIndex concurrently. For file-backed indexes both calls use the same directory and call bleve.New on it at the same time; for memory indexes the later `b.cache[key] = idx` overwrites the first. This can cause index creation failures/corruption and can drop watch updates applied to the overwritten index. Add a per-key lock/singleflight, or re-check and serialize index creation for the same key before creating the bleve index.

findings.title: Postgres coverage removed from storage-server startup test
findings.body: The test now unconditionally skips Postgres, removing coverage for a production database at exactly the startup path changed by this PR (resource server initialization moved into the constructor). Because the skip is global rather than CI-specific, a Postgres-specific regression in startup initialization will not be caught. Fix the underlying Postgres issue or scope any temporary skip to CI only.
